cohort: Pregnant women who underwent a labor trial at the Second Hospital of West China University of Sichuan University and practiced either the warm and calm breathing pattern or the Lamaze breathing technique.
finding: The warm and calm breathing pattern significantly reduced the incidence of fetal intrauterine distress, emergency cesarean delivery, forceps-assisted delivery, episiotomy, third- and fourth-degree perineal tears, and postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: The warm and calm breathing pattern reduced the incidence of emergency cesarean delivery and forceps-assisted delivery.
